_help: Hand-written promotional angles. Each is a different reason a stranger might click, paired with real gameplay media. {link} is replaced by a demo link tagged for that platform and angle (scripts/angle_bank.py). Every X text is checked by tests/test_angle_bank.py against the same post rules as the autopilot, game vocabulary, length limits and similarity to every other angle. Facts used: RINGSHIFT_KNOWLEDGE.md (mechanic behaviour, platform, 110 levels) and the level/lock counts visible in each asset's own HUD.

angles.name: The whole game in one rule
angles.why: Strangers need to know what they would be doing. One plain sentence, then the trailer shows it.
angles.x:
Rotate the rings. Every lock on the rim has to be lit at the same time, or none of them count.

That's the whole rule. 110 levels to break it.

{link}

#puzzlegame #indiegame #Ringshift
angles.bluesky: Rotate the rings until every lock on the rim is lit at the same time. That's the whole rule, and there are 110 levels of it. Free in the browser: {link}
angles.shorts_title: Rotate the rings until every lock lights at once #puzzle #indiegame

angles.name: The rule that makes it a puzzle
angles.why: A genuine design twist that puzzle fans like to think about.
angles.x:
A ring's own mirror can never bend that ring's beam. They rotate together.

So every piece only matters for the OTHER rings. That one rule is the puzzle.

{link}

#gamedesign #puzzlegame #Ringshift
angles.bluesky: In Ringshift a ring's own mirror never bends that ring's beam, because they rotate together. Every piece only matters for the other rings. Free demo: {link}
angles.shorts_title: Why a ring's own mirror can't bend its own beam #gamedesign

angles.name: The beam that keeps going
angles.why: Echo portal is unusual: the original beam continues while a copy appears elsewhere.
angles.x:
A portal moves a beam. An echo portal copies it: one beam comes out the paired mouth and the original keeps going.

Hard 25 uses both.

{link}
